evidence.note: Deliberately set up a modular staged pipeline: token.rs, lexer.rs, preprocessor.rs, parser.rs, ast.rs, sema.rs, codegen.rs, main.rs — distinct lexer/parser/analysis/codegen stages, matching the anchor-5 'coherent staged pipeline'.

Representations were improvised, not designed up front: initial AST failed to compile (Struct/Union had 2 fields where 4 needed), and Type::Func had to be reworked from Vec<Type> to Vec<(String,Type)> mid-build — shows type representation not fully anticipated.

A real lvalue vs rvalue design exists via separate codegen paths ge() (rvalue) and glv() (address/lvalue), a hard-part representation beyond anchor 5 — but its foundations had bugs (pointer subscript in glv) discovered reactively via failing tests rather than designed correctly up front.

Type-aware sized codegen with register-width helpers (ld()/rw() keyed on type size) and struct layout with size/align/offset (compute_locals) — genuine representations for the hard parts, indicating design above a bare 5.

Incomplete-type resolution (self-referential structs) was added late by threading new struct/union maps into codegen — a representational capability bolted on reactively rather than absorbed by the original design, so it falls short of anchor 8's disruption-free composition.

reasoning: The agent clearly cleared anchor 5: a coherent staged pipeline with distinct lexer/parser/analysis/codegen and reasonable AST/type/scope representations. It reached partway toward anchor 8 by including genuine hard-part representations — a Type enum, an lvalue/rvalue ge()/glv() split, struct layout with size/align/offset, and type-aware sized codegen. But these representations were improvised, failed to compile initially, were repeatedly reworked (Type::Func, incomplete-type resolution added late), and their rationale was reactive rather than made explicit up front, so it does not meet anchor 8's 'deliberately designed so later features slot in with minimal disruption.' That places it at a 6, between 5 and 8.
